plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated interval session for speed development.
Incorporates hill-specific training to build durability and strength on trails.
Includes strength training to improve muscular endurance, beneficial for trail running.
Provides a more balanced approach to training, incorporating speed, endurance, and strength.
plan_b_advantages: Longer long run (123 minutes vs 102 minutes) may contribute to greater overall endurance.
Includes cross-training, which can provide a lower-impact aerobic stimulus and aid recovery.
Tempo run may improve lactate threshold, which can be beneficial for sustained effort.
reasoning: Given the goal of becoming a faster trail runner, Plan A appears to be the better choice. While both plans incorporate essential elements like long runs and rest days, Plan A includes a dedicated interval session, which is crucial for developing speed and power – key components of faster trail running. Plan B focuses more on sustained aerobic effort and cross-training, which are important for endurance but less directly impactful on speed. The inclusion of hill-specific training and strength work in Plan A also better addresses the demands of trail running.
